closed.prompt:
The reference image is a finished prop (a workbench) from the SAME workshop in the SAME game. Take from it ONLY its drawing STYLE: the ink line weight, the flat cel colouring, the painted wear, the finish and the camera height. Take NOTHING of its shape or subject. Do NOT draw a table, a bench or anything from it.

SUBJECT: ONE old steel mechanic's TOOLBOX standing alone, a small portable hand toolbox (about the size of a shoebox), seen from a level side view very slightly from above, its long front side facing us. It has a hip-roof (barn-top) lid with a folding wire carry handle lying flat along the ridge, two brass draw-latches on the front, brass corner caps, and a line of rivets. It is painted in deep OXBLOOD RED enamel, chipped and worn down to bare grey steel along every edge and corner, with a few rust blooms and one dent in the left end. The lid is NOT fully shut: it sits a finger's width AJAR, and along the whole seam between lid and body a thin line of bright CYAN light leaks out, as if something lit is shut inside. The cyan light catches the brass latches and the lower edge of the lid right beside the seam. The light stays ON the toolbox's own surfaces: no glow halo in the air around it, no light rays.

PROPORTION: the toolbox is about 1.7 times as wide as it is tall, and fills about 70% of the frame width. A squat heavy box, NOT a tall chest, NOT a treasure chest, NOT a crate, NOT a cabinet with drawers.

RENDER: clean confident ink linework, flat cel colour with soft painted light, one warm amber lamp key light from the upper right, exactly like the reference prop. PALETTE in words: oxblood red enamel, bare grey steel at the chips, dull brass latches and corners, one line of cyan seam light.

PLATE RULES: pure flat black background (#000000) everywhere that is not the toolbox; the whole toolbox inside the frame with clear margin on all four sides; nothing else in the picture: no tools beside it, no floor, no ground line, no cast shadow, no text, no letters, no numbers, no logo, no watermark.

open.prompt:
The reference image is a finished game prop: an old oxblood-red steel toolbox with a thin line of cyan light leaking from under its lid. Draw the SAME toolbox again — the same object, the same camera, the same size and position in the frame, the same ink linework and flat cel colour, the same chipped red enamel, the same brass latches, brass corner caps and rivets, the same dent — with ONE change: the lid is now swung fully OPEN.

THE CHANGE: the barn-top lid has been lifted and stands upright, hinged along the back edge of the box, leaning slightly backwards, its inside face (bare grey steel, a little rusty) towards us. The two brass latches hang loose on the front. Inside the open box we see an EMPTY dark steel tray: nothing in it. There is NO cyan light anywhere any more — whatever was glowing inside has been taken out. No glow, no light line.

Do not redesign the box, do not change its colour, do not move it in the frame: the lower body of the box must sit exactly where it sits in the reference.

PLATE RULES: pure flat black background (#000000) everywhere that is not the toolbox; the whole toolbox including the raised lid inside the frame with clear margin; nothing else in the picture: no tools, no floor, no ground line, no cast shadow, no text, no letters, no logo, no watermark.
